evals.prompt: I have two separate claude.ai artifact requests today. Request A: a single static counter component — just a number on screen, a plus button, and a minus button, no routing between views, no state beyond the counter value, and no shadcn/ui components needed. Request B: a project-tracker dashboard with three client-side routed views (Board, Calendar, Settings), state shared across all three views, and it needs shadcn/ui Dialog, Tabs, and DataTable components. Should I use the web-artifacts-builder skill for Request A, Request B, both, or neither? Explain your reasoning for each request separately.
evals.expected_output: The skill's own frontmatter description scopes exactly this decision: "Use for complex artifacts requiring state management, routing, or shadcn/ui components - not for simple single-file HTML/JSX artifacts." For Request A, none of the three named triggers apply — there is no routing, no state beyond a single counter value, and no shadcn/ui components — so it is a simple single-file HTML/JSX artifact and the skill explicitly says it is not for that case; the correct answer is to build it directly as a plain HTML/JSX artifact without initializing the skill's project (no `scripts/init-artifact.sh`, no bundling step). For Request B, all three named triggers are present at once: routing (three client-side routed views), state management (state shared across the views), and shadcn/ui components (Dialog, Tabs, DataTable) — this is precisely the "complex artifacts requiring state management, routing, or shadcn/ui components" the description calls out, so the skill applies and the agent should follow its 5-step process starting with `scripts/init-artifact.sh`.
expectations: Agent explicitly recommends against using the web-artifacts-builder skill for Request A, on the grounds that it is a simple single-file HTML/JSX artifact with none of the skill's triggering conditions.
Agent quotes or closely paraphrases the description's scoping line, e.g. 'not for simple single-file HTML/JSX artifacts.'
Agent explicitly recommends using the web-artifacts-builder skill for Request B.
Agent identifies at least two of the three specific triggers present in Request B (routing, shared/global state, shadcn/ui components) as the reason the skill applies.
Agent does not propose running scripts/init-artifact.sh or otherwise invoking the skill's workflow for Request A.
The response clearly differentiates the two requests rather than giving one blanket yes/no answer to both.

evals.prompt: I'm about to build a claude.ai artifact using the web-artifacts-builder skill — a multi-page settings app with client-side routing and a shadcn/ui Tabs component. My plan: skip straight to writing App.tsx and my route components by hand in a brand-new empty folder, and once the React code looks right, just paste the raw .tsx source files into the chat as the artifact so the user can see it. Does this plan follow the skill correctly? Fix anything that's wrong.
evals.expected_output: The skill defines an exact, numbered process: "1. Initialize the frontend repo using scripts/init-artifact.sh 2. Develop your artifact by editing the generated code 3. Bundle all code into a single HTML file using scripts/bundle-artifact.sh 4. Display artifact to user 5. (Optional) Test the artifact." The plan violates step 1 by writing files from scratch in an empty folder instead of running `bash scripts/init-artifact.sh <project-name>` first; step 2 explicitly says to develop "by editing the generated code," which presupposes code was already generated by the init script, not authored from a blank folder. The plan also skips step 3 and step 4: pasting raw .tsx source into chat is not what step 4 describes ("share the bundled HTML file in conversation with the user"), and it bypasses running `bash scripts/bundle-artifact.sh`, which is documented to create "bundle.html - a self-contained artifact with all JavaScript, CSS, and dependencies inlined. This file can be directly shared in Claude conversations as an artifact." The corrected plan is: run scripts/init-artifact.sh to initialize the project, edit the generated code, run scripts/bundle-artifact.sh to produce bundle.html, and share that bundle.html file with the user — not the raw .tsx sources.
expectations: Agent identifies that the plan skips Step 1 (running scripts/init-artifact.sh) and flags this as incorrect.
Agent explains that Step 2 ('Develop your artifact by editing the generated code') means editing code the init script generated, not writing new files from scratch in an empty folder.
Agent identifies that pasting raw .tsx source directly into the chat skips the required bundling step (scripts/bundle-artifact.sh).
Agent states the artifact that should actually be shared is bundle.html, describing it as self-contained with all JavaScript, CSS, and dependencies inlined — not raw source files.
Agent presents the corrected sequence in order: initialize, then develop, then bundle, then display (optionally test), matching the skill's 5 numbered steps.

evals.prompt: Here's a design draft for a claude.ai artifact I'm about to build with web-artifacts-builder: every section on the page — hero, features, pricing, and footer — uses a centered layout, the hero section has a purple-to-blue gradient background, all text on the page uses the Inter font, and every card and button on the page shares the exact same 12px rounded corners. Before I start implementing this in code, review the design against the skill's design guidelines and tell me what needs to change.
evals.expected_output: The skill's Design & Style Guidelines section states: "VERY IMPORTANT: To avoid what is often referred to as 'AI slop', avoid using excessive centered layouts, purple gradients, uniform rounded corners, and Inter font." The draft hits all four flagged patterns: centering every section (hero, features, pricing, footer) matches "excessive centered layouts"; the purple-to-blue gradient hero matches "purple gradients"; the site-wide Inter font matches "Inter font" directly; and identical 12px corners on every card and button match "uniform rounded corners." A correct review names all four as violations of this explicitly VERY IMPORTANT guideline and recommends the design be reworked away from them, without inventing a specific replacement font, palette, or corner-radius scheme as if the skill itself prescribed one — SKILL.md only states what to avoid, not what to use instead.
expectations: Agent flags the purple-to-blue gradient hero background as violating the guideline against 'purple gradients.'
Agent flags the site-wide Inter font as violating the guideline against 'Inter font.'
Agent flags the uniform 12px rounded corners on every card/button as violating the guideline against 'uniform rounded corners.'
Agent flags the fully centered layout across all four page sections as violating the guideline against 'excessive centered layouts.'
Agent characterizes this as a VERY IMPORTANT guideline from the skill (the 'AI slop' rule), not a minor stylistic nitpick.
Agent does not attribute a specific alternative font, gradient/color, or corner-radius value to the skill as though SKILL.md prescribes a replacement — it only names what to avoid.

evals.prompt: I ran scripts/init-artifact.sh, edited the generated code, and now I want to run scripts/bundle-artifact.sh to produce the final artifact for the user. But I just noticed my project's root directory doesn't have an index.html file anymore — I deleted it earlier while cleaning up files I thought were unused. Can I go ahead and run the bundle script now, or is this a problem?
evals.expected_output: Step 3 of the skill states an explicit prerequisite: "Requirements: Your project must have an index.html in the root directory." Since the project's index.html was deleted, this requirement is not met, and running scripts/bundle-artifact.sh at this point is not documented to work — the correct answer flags the missing index.html as a blocker for bundling, not something safe to skip past. The agent should tell the user to restore or recreate an index.html at the project root before running `bash scripts/bundle-artifact.sh`, since the skill gives no indication that the bundling step (which "Installs bundling dependencies," "Creates .parcelrc config," "Builds with Parcel," and "Inlines all assets into single HTML using html-inline") will generate a missing index.html on its own.
expectations: Agent identifies the missing index.html at the project root as a blocker for running scripts/bundle-artifact.sh.
Agent explicitly cites or closely paraphrases the requirement 'Your project must have an index.html in the root directory.'
Agent does not tell the user to proceed with bundling as-is despite the missing file.
Agent recommends restoring or recreating index.html at the project root before running the bundle script.

Agent does not claim that scripts/bundle-artifact.sh will automatically generate a missing index.html, since SKILL.md's description of what the script does (install dependencies, create .parcelrc, build with Parcel, inline assets) does not say this.

evals.prompt: I just finished running scripts/bundle-artifact.sh and I have bundle.html ready. Before showing it to the user, I want to spin up Playwright to click through every button and verify the UI renders correctly, just to be safe. Is that the right move at this point?
evals.expected_output: Step 5 of the skill is explicit that testing is optional and should not happen by default before the artifact is shown: "Note: This is a completely optional step. Only perform if necessary or requested... In general, avoid testing the artifact upfront as it adds latency between the request and when the finished artifact can be seen. Test later, after presenting the artifact, if requested or if issues arise." Since bundling (step 3) is already done, the correct next action per step 4 is to "share the bundled HTML file in conversation with the user so they can view it as an artifact" first, and only run Playwright-style testing afterward if the user asks for it or a problem turns up — not proactively before the user has seen anything. Playwright/Puppeteer are named as acceptable tools for this optional step ("built-in tools like Playwright or Puppeteer"), so testing itself is not wrong, only doing it upfront instead of after presenting the artifact.
expectations: Agent advises against running Playwright before showing the artifact to the user, i.e. does not endorse the plan as-is.
Agent cites that testing is 'a completely optional step' to be performed 'only if necessary or requested.'
Agent cites the explicit reasoning that testing upfront 'adds latency between the request and when the finished artifact can be seen.'
Agent recommends sharing/displaying bundle.html with the user first (Step 4) before running any tests.
Agent states testing should happen after presenting the artifact, if requested or if issues arise — not proactively beforehand.
Agent does not claim testing is forbidden outright; it frames Playwright as acceptable later, matching the skill naming 'Playwright or Puppeteer' as valid optional tools.

evals.prompt: I just ran scripts/init-artifact.sh for my new claude.ai artifact project. Before I start editing code, tell me exactly what this setup already gives me — the frontend stack and everything init-artifact.sh configured — so I know what I don't need to install or configure myself.
evals.expected_output: The skill states the overall stack directly: "Stack: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + Parcel (bundling) + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui." Step 1 then lists exactly what the init script sets up: "React + TypeScript (via Vite)", "Tailwind CSS 3.4.1 with shadcn/ui theming system", "Path aliases (@/) configured", "40+ shadcn/ui components pre-installed", "All Radix UI dependencies included", "Parcel configured for bundling (via .parcelrc)", and "Node 18+ compatibility (auto-detects and pins Vite version)". A correct answer recalls these specific facts precisely — including the Tailwind version number, the exact component count, and the path alias syntax — rather than a generic 'it sets up React and Tailwind' summary, and does not introduce tools or frameworks the skill never mentions (e.g. Next.js, Webpack, styled-components).
expectations: Agent states the stack as React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + Parcel (bundling) + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui, matching the skill's Stack line.
Agent specifies Tailwind CSS 3.4.1 together with the shadcn/ui theming system, not just a generic 'Tailwind CSS' mention.
Agent mentions that path aliases (@/) are already configured.
Agent mentions that 40+ shadcn/ui components are pre-installed, and that all Radix UI dependencies are included.
Agent mentions that Parcel is configured for bundling via .parcelrc.

Agent mentions Node 18+ compatibility with auto-detection/pinning of the Vite version, and does not invent unlisted tools or frameworks (e.g. Next.js, Webpack, styled-components) as part of the setup.
